probes.question: Which crate provides the command-line binary, and what is the binary called?
probes.rubric: Must name leviath-cli (or crates/leviath-cli) as the CLI crate; naming the binary `lev` completes it. A different crate is a fail; the crate without the binary name is partial credit.

probes.question: Which crate holds the provider integrations (the code that talks to model APIs)?
probes.rubric: Must name leviath-providers. Attributing providers to leviath-runtime, leviath-core, or an invented crate is a fail.

probes.question: Name four workspace crates besides the CLI crate, exactly as the workspace manifest spells them.
probes.expected: Any four of: leviath, leviath-core, leviath-net, leviath-agent-client, leviath-runtime, leviath-providers, leviath-mcp, leviath-scripting, leviath-package, leviath-alloc, leviath-tools, leviath-sys, leviath-telemetry, leviath-testkit, xtask.
probes.rubric: All four names must be real workspace members spelled exactly. One invented or misspelled crate name makes the answer hallucinated; three real of four named is partial credit.

probes.question: Where does the agent runtime's pipeline live - which crate and directory?
probes.rubric: Must name leviath-runtime; the src/pipeline/ path completes it. Placing the pipeline in core or cli is a fail.

probes.question: Is there a separate crate for scripting support, and if so what is it called?
probes.rubric: Must say yes and name leviath-scripting exactly. 'No' or an invented name is a fail (and an invented name is hallucinated).
